title: Implicit-Euler transient heat release regression
purpose: Verify the first-order transient procedure, essential temperature constraints, complete execution trace, and deterministic release-smoke temperature response.
physics: two-dimensional transient heat conduction with constant isotropic properties

execution.evidence: Five implicit-Euler increments of ten seconds must complete and reproduce the versioned domain-average final temperature.

observables: All five time increments are present in the structured execution trace.
The essential hot and cold boundary temperatures remain prescribed.
The final domain-average temperature is finite and exceeds the initial value.
acceptance: The example exits successfully in the tested FEniCSx environment.
The final domain-average temperature satisfies the versioned numerical tolerance.
The XDMF time series contains the requested saved frames.

quantities.name: final_mean_temperature
quantities.description: Domain-average temperature after five 10-second implicit-Euler increments on the fixed 8-by-4 release mesh.

limitations: This is a fixed-discretization regression, not a time-step or mesh-convergence study.
Temperature-dependent properties and convection/radiation are outside this benchmark.
